newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday with all later-maturing contracts breaching the 20,000 support level on weak sentiment despite last Friday's gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra- day low of 19,950 yuan ($2,403) per tonne, down 90 yuan. It opened at a high of 20,050.
October fell 110 to 20,220 yuan, November 160 to 20,000, December 130 to 19,980, January 90 to 19,950 and March 90 to 19,980.
Combined volume rose to 18,950 tonnes from 9,160.
The copper contracts opened little changed and mostly at their intra-day highs but long liquidation and hedging selling pushed them down for most of the session.
Traders said investors were cautious about building positions as the LME was still consolidating in a narrow range despite last Friday's gains.

"Weak sentiment dominated today's trading, because most investors believe the LME did not give a clear direction," one trader said. "Domestic hedging selling was largely due to poor mid- and long-term fundamentals."
Traders said the short-term trend was still not clear despite the fall of all later-maturing contracts below the key support 20,000 yuan level.
"There was no panic selling today after copper breached the 20,000 yuan level," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move around 20,000 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mostly down. October was unchanged at 13,950 yuan, November fell 20 to 13,800 and December 30 to 13,700. Combined volume fell to 720 tonnes from 870.
